messages:
Maya R: ran a quick cross-cloud p95 sweep for the new quantized 7B on identical a100-80gb SKUs across AWS/GCP/Azure. results are weird, posting summary.
Raj P: curious — same driver/CUDA on all three?
Maya R: nope. tried three stacks:
- aws: 520.61.05 / cuda 11.8
- gcp: 520.56.06 / cuda 11.8
- azure: 515.65.01 / cuda 11.7
Sylvie: small driver diffs can cause kernel selection changes, especially for int8 kernels. did you see any kernel mismatch logs?
Maya R: yes, on GCP we see fallback to matmul_fp32 for the int8 path occasionally. logs:
```
[2026-03-10T12:04:21Z] kernel_select: attempted int8_gemm_sm80, fallback->fp32_sgemm (heuristic latency>=threshold)
```
Raj P: that would blow up p95. what's the test profile? bs=8, seq=1024, streaming off?
Maya R: bs=8, seq=512 for this sweep, streaming=on, KV cache warm. p50 roughly same but p95/Azure and p95/GCP spike compared to AWS.
Tom K: numbers? rough p95 tokens/sec or latency?
Maya R: latency p95 for 1-token step (autoregressive):
- AWS (520.61.05): 18.6ms
- GCP (520.56.06): 27.9ms (with spikes to 110ms)
- AZURE (515.65.01): 32.2ms (sporadic 200ms)
Sylvie: spikes that big usually come from either fallback kernels or CPU-side throttles (pci-e pause) or driver reset retries. check dmesg for GPU timeouts.
Maya R: looked — GCP nodes show repeated nvlink timeouts and a few gpu_recovery messages, example:
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
```
Raj P: oh nice. did you repro with MIG disabled? MIG can affect scheduler decisions.
Maya R: disabled MIG on one repro run — p95 improved on GCP but still worse than AWS. also saw different cublasLt paths selected when MIG off.
Sylvie: this screams subtle firmware/BIOS or platform PCI patience differences between clouds. driver minor versions trigger different heuristics in kernel selection.
Tom K: can you paste the perf command and env used so infra can repro?
Maya R: sure — run command we used:
```
LD_PRELOAD=/opt/redwood/quant_kernels.so \ 
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \ 
python -m rwinference.bench --model r7b-q8 --batch 8 --seq 512 --streams 4 --warmup 200 --iters 200
```
Infra-bot: repro request created: INF-2391. Attach perf logs and dmesg output to the ticket.
Raj P: next steps: (1) repro with kernel tracing enabled to capture cublasLt selection, (2) test with cuda 11.9/driver 525.x if available, (3) run with small bs=1 to isolate tail from batching noise.
Maya R: will do 1+3 tomorrow. also trying quantization knob: q8->q4_0 on GCP to see if smaller kernels avoid fallback.
Sylvie: also try forcing algorithm override if possible in our runtime to pin the int8 gemm kernel and see if stability improves.
Maya R: noted. I'll upload the CSV with per-step latencies and kernel names to INF-2391. thanks all :thumbsup:
